newsitem.title: USA: Conn. single family home prices rise quickly - paper.
newsitem.headline: Conn. single family home prices rise quickly - paper.

text.p: Prices for single-family homes in Connecticut rose at their fastest clip in three years during the third quarter, the Hartford Courant reported on Thursday, citing a University of Connecticut index.

The Center for Real Estate and Urban Economic Studies at the University, which surveyed sales in 31 towns, found the average statewide sale price of a "mid-priced" house rose 2.1 percent to $206,000 from $201,800 in the year-ago period.
Prices of lower-priced houses rose 1.5 percent to $162,500 from $160,100. And high-priced homes fetched 3.2 percent more, rising to $266,200 from $257,900, the Courant said.
Before prices began recovering in the 1995 fourth quarter, the average price of houses had fallen for eight consectuive quarters, the paper said.
However, prices have continued to fall in Hartford, though some coummunities in the area registered gains, as did New Britain, it added.
